text: Four groups have to cooperate for these solutions to work. One of them has far more to give up than the rest.
bullets: Typists lose the job of typing summaries each morning. Their work moves to checking drafts, and they need to hear that first.
Doctors are asked for nothing beyond the round they already do. If a new form or a second round appears, that promise is broken.
Your Head of Operations signs off but is not on the ward. Without that yes, the change fails on its first busy day.
chat.pointer: Each sheet shows what that group gives up and what we ask of them.
chat.invite: Next is what it costs, set against what is at stake. Shall we go there?
chat.note: The resistance sits with the typists, not the doctors.
prompts: How do we tell the typists?

blocks.title: Who has to say yes
blocks.deck: Four groups do the work. One person approves it.

doers.said: Summaries are typed the next morning.
doers.gives_up: Typing every summary from the doctor’s notes
doers.ask: Check each draft instead: same hours, lighter work

doers.said: We won’t sign a final summary at night, but will sign an early one.
doers.gives_up: Nothing. They decide on the round, as today.
doers.ask: No extra time beyond the round they already do

doers.gives_up: Doing discharge work in the morning rush
doers.ask: Start the checklist that night, not next morning

doers.gives_up: Waiting for the morning to start the bill
doers.ask: Bill and insurance request done by 9 PM

approver.why: Owns the staff and the budget, not the daily ward work
approver.fails: The new hours are dropped the first time the wards get busy
